notes:
Summary: IDEWave builds a JetBrains family plugin (IntelliJ/PyCharm) that combines a local indexer with a cloud model for heavy completions. They want local-first policy: small queries resolved from on-device index, fall back to server for larger context/LLM completions.

Key product asks:
- Low-latency streaming (editor suggestions within 50-80ms ideally).
- Model/version pinning per customer so enterprise customers can pin to specific quantized variants.
- Local indexing support + cache invalidation hooks (file system watch + project-aware TTL).
- Ability to provide a private connector (on-prem or VPC) that hosts the model for regulated enterprise customers.
- Granular audit logs and retention controls for code snippets and telemetry.

Technical notes from SE call:
- Prefer a small on-device index (Lucene) and a tiny local LSP process for tokenization; only send requests to Redwood when the local candidate set < threshold or for multi-file synthesis.
- Concern about token leakage from file context; asked about KMS integration and masking/PII scrubbers.
- Wants streaming websocket SDK for JetBrains plugin (current plugin SDK is Java/Kotlin based).

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "We need suggestions to feel instantaneous — anything >100ms is noticeable in-editor"
- "Enterprises will require a dedicated private footprint, and they will insist on version pinning for reproducibility."

POC ask:
- Provide a POC with: 1) a hosted inference route with streaming websocket sample for JetBrains, 2) a small private Docker image that can be deployed in their staging VPC for latency tests, 3) docs for model pinning API.

Commercial/contract notes:
- Price sensitivity at SMB plugin partners — but will upsell enterprise customers for private deployment and SSO.

Open questions:
- How granular are rollout controls for specific model variants at route-level?
- Can we offer a local cache library (BSD/MIT) that integrates with their existing indexer?

Next steps (short):
- SE to produce POC artifact and Jenkins pipeline by 2026-03-12.
- Legal to respond on Data Processing Addendum (DPA) — customer requested 2-week SLA on review.
- Follow-up demo scheduled 2026-03-12.
